field.organic_snippet: Admins can now view all their agents in a single, centralized registry providing a unified view of agent adoption, activity, and agent health.

F1.quote: An AI registry is a live catalog of every AI model, agent, and use case with ownership, risk tier, and regulatory status.
F1.claim: an AI registry defined: a live catalog of AI models, agents and use cases with ownership, risk tier and regulatory status

F2.locus: the page, 'What is an AI registry?'
F2.quote: An AI registry is the central record of every AI system your company runs — including trained models, bought-in agents, internal copilots, and AI features SaaS vendors activated last quarter.
F2.claim: the AI registry as the central record of every AI system a company runs

F3.quote: An AI registry prevents that from happening again. It puts every AI system in one place, with the owner, the risk tier, and the regulatory status attached to each entry.
F3.claim: the registry's function: every AI system in one place with owner, risk tier, regulatory status

F4.quote: EU AI Act Article 12 requires high-risk systems to support automatic event logging — static spreadsheets will not comply.
F4.claim: the regulatory driver: EU AI Act Article 12 event logging

F5.quote: A 12-field schema maps directly to EU AI Act Annex IV, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC 42001 obligations.
F5.claim: a 12-field schema mapped to EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001

F6.quote: As organizations scale AI initiatives, AI assets are increasingly created across multiple heterogeneous environments such as Google Vertex AI, Azure and Databricks.
F6.claim: AI assets fragmented across environments such as Vertex AI, Azure, Databricks
F6.checked_against: saved page text collibra.txt (sha256 aee6b2b35a091341…), whitespace-normalised

F7.locus: the page, 'What's new: Unified AI registry'
F7.quote: It acts as a single inventory where teams can track AI use cases, models and agents while maintaining governance context such as ownership, lifecycle status and trust metrics.
F7.claim: Collibra's unified AI registry: a single inventory of AI use cases, models and agents with governance context
F7.checked_against: saved page text collibra.txt (sha256 aee6b2b35a091341…), whitespace-normalised

F8.quote: An AI Registry is a centralized system of record for all your organization's AI assets — models, agents, systems, use cases, and third-party vendors.
F8.claim: an AI Registry: a centralized system of record for an organization's AI assets

F9.quote: trail automates this AI intake process through integrations with your existing asset inventories, GRC platforms, and the environments where AI is actively built
F9.claim: trail automates AI intake through integrations (GRC platforms, asset inventories, build environments)

F10.quote: It's the foundation for any effective AI governance program.
F10.claim: the registry as the foundation of AI governance

F11.quote: Agent Registry is a centralized catalog that lets you store, discover, and govern agentic components , such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, tools, standalone skills, and AI agents, within Google Cloud.
F11.claim: Google Cloud's Agent Registry: a catalog of agentic components within Google Cloud

F12.quote: By consolidating these agents, MCP servers, skills, and endpoints, Agent Registry addresses common challenges in complex AI deployments, such as fragmented tool access, isolated data, and redundant implementations.
F12.claim: the Agent Registry's purpose: consolidation against fragmentation

F13.quote: Google AI Overviews show up on a large share of search queries now, and that share has kept climbing since the feature rolled out.
F13.claim: AI Overviews appear on a large and growing share of queries

F14.quote: Two working approaches handle this: a Playwright-based browser scraper that renders the full DOM and extracts text blocks with source references, and a SERP API that returns the same data as structured JSON without any browser overhead.
F14.claim: two approaches to extracting AI Overviews: a Playwright scraper and a SERP API

F15.locus: the page, 'Three States of AI Overviews'
F15.quote: Most AIO scraping attempts fail because they send a single HTTP request and get back an empty container.
F15.claim: limit: deferred Overviews defeat single-request scraping

F16.quote: The EASIEST Way to Track Google AI Overviews (Find Ranking Opportunities)
F16.claim: a video on tracking AI Overviews to find ranking opportunities

F17.quote: Monitor how Google's AI Overviews display your brand on mobile search. Real 4G/5G carrier IPs show exactly what users see - no datacenter detection, no filtered results.
F17.claim: mobile-proxy monitoring of how AI Overviews display a brand

F18.quote: Track Google AI Overviews for free: see whether Google shows one for a keyword, which sites it cites and in what order, and whether your domain is one of them.
F18.claim: Honeyb's free AI Overview tracker: whether an Overview appears, which sites it cites, whether yours is one

F19.quote: Each keyword is one Google search from the United States, desktop, in English, with the asynchronously loaded AI Overview included. We record whether an overview appeared, every source it cited in the order Google listed them, the brands its text links to, and the organic top 10 for comparison.
F19.claim: the method: one US desktop English search per keyword; sources cited in order and the organic top 10 recorded

F20.quote: The domain in position one is cited 48% of the time and the share falls with every place down the page, to 26% by the last row. Meanwhile 40% of overviews lead with a source that is not on page one at all.
F20.claim: finding: organic rank one is cited 48% of the time; 40% of Overviews lead with a source not on page one

F21.quote: The limit is the one every single capture has: overviews change between days, by location and by account. A monthly snapshot shows the shape of a query, not its day-to-day movement.
F21.claim: limit: Overviews change by day, location and account; a monthly snapshot shows a query's shape

F22.quote: Effective AI Overview tracking requires monitoring a defined query set at a fixed weekly cadence, recording citation sources historically, and detecting competitive shifts before they consolidate.
F22.claim: effective tracking: a defined query set at weekly cadence, citation sources recorded historically

F23.quote: Google Search Console doesn't isolate AI Overview clicks, and standard rank trackers measure organic position, not citation presence.
F23.claim: Search Console does not isolate AI Overview clicks; rank trackers measure organic position, not citation presence

F24.quote: Manually checking whether you appear in AI Overviews is not tracking. It's a snapshot of one query, on one device, at one moment, and by tomorrow, the citation could be someone else's.
F24.claim: a manual check is a snapshot, not tracking

F25.quote: AI Overview tracking helps you understand when AI Overviews appear for your keywords, whether your website is cited, which pages and competitors are featured and how your visibility changes over time.
F25.claim: AI Overview tracking defined by its uses: appearance, citation, competitors, visibility over time

F26.locus: the page, 'A different set of cited sources'
F26.quote: AI Overview citations don't necessarily match the pages ranking in the organic top 10. BrightEdge found that only about 17% of sources cited in AI Overviews also ranked in the organic top 10, showing that traditional rankings alone don't capture all of the pages Google surfaces in AI Overviews.
F26.claim: AI Overview citations diverge from the organic top 10 (BrightEdge: about 17%)

F27.locus: the page (the card's snippet), 'Google Universal vs. Google Search + AIO'
F27.quote: Google Universal picks up AI Overviews as part of a standard SERP crawl, which works well in most cases but can occasionally return incomplete or missing source URLs for that feature specifically.
F27.claim: limit: a standard SERP crawl can miss AI Overview source URLs; a dedicated mechanism closes the gap

F28.quote: Google AI Overviews are reshaping how informational queries get answered, and the data inside them, including the AI-generated summary, the cited sources, and the source URLs, has become some of the most valuable SEO data on the web.
F28.claim: AI Overview data as valuable SEO data

F29.quote: There are four ways to scrape Google AI Overviews: pre-built templates , AI Chrome extensions, commercial SERP APIs, and general scraping APIs with custom parsing.
F29.claim: four ways to scrape AI Overviews

F30.quote: A Google AI Overview Tracker monitors whether your keywords trigger AI-generated summaries in Google search, identifies every website cited inside those summaries, tracks their positions over time, and generates automated reports — giving complete visibility into AI search performance that Google Search Console does not provide.
